title: Add integration test harness for KMS failure modes (timeouts/throttling) + retry/latency assertions
author: Sahana Iyer
release_notes: Adds CI/staging integration tests that simulate KMS timeout + throttling and assert retry budgets/latency caps/failure propagation for envelope decrypt paths.
description: Context: As part of the KMS hardening initiative (ENG-4821/ENG-4825) we need repeatable, non-flaky coverage for the most common real-world failure modes we’ve seen (timeouts and throttling) and guardrails to prevent retry amplification. This PR introduces an integration-test harness that can deterministically inject KMS failures and validate that our KMS wrapper obeys configured budgets (max retries + max wall-clock) and that upstream services surface the correct error category without masking (e.g., Throttling vs Timeout vs AccessDenied). What’s included: (1) A small “kms-fault-injector” sidecar used only in integration tests (runs in docker-compose and the CI integration job). It proxies KMS requests and can inject (a) fixed latency, (b) probabilistic timeouts (connection stall), and (c) throttling responses (AWS-style ThrottlingException / HTTP 429 equivalent) based on per-test configuration. (2) New integration tests for envelope decrypt paths in the control-plane and data-plane adapters that cover: timeout -> retry with jitter -> fail fast within latency cap; throttling -> bounded retries -> correct error taxonomy; and “mixed” failure where first N requests throttle then succeed, asserting the wrapper eventually succeeds without exceeding retry budget. (3) Assertions for total wall-clock budget and retry counts using emitted metrics/spans from the wrapper: kms.client.attempts (counter), kms.client.latency_ms (histogram), kms.client.errors{category=...} (counter). These assertions are done by reading the local in-memory test metrics exporter (not scraping Prometheus) to keep tests hermetic. (4) A CI job wiring (integration-kms-failure-modes) that runs these tests in parallel with other integration suites, gated on main and release/*, and skips on fork PRs (requires docker service). How to run locally: `make itest-kms-failure-modes` (requires docker). Notes/constraints: This is AWS-mode only for now; the harness is intentionally provider-agnostic at the proxy layer, but the error-shape fixtures currently match AWS responses. We’ll extend with GCP/Azure once those wrappers land behind the same error taxonomy (ENG-4822). We intentionally avoid testing circuit-breaker behavior here; that is covered in ENG-4824/PR-18449. Risk: Low product risk (test-only code paths), moderate flake risk; mitigations include deterministic seeds, fixed injection windows, and conservative latency thresholds. Evidence: This PR adds regression coverage for SUP-19377 patterns (intermittent 5xx correlated with KMS throttling) and enforces the retry cap/latency cap behavior agreed in ADR-007.
commits: test(kms): add fault-injector proxy + docker-compose wiring for integration tests
test(kms): add throttling + timeout scenarios for envelope decrypt integration suite
test(metrics): add in-memory exporter helpers for asserting attempt counts and error categories
ci: add integration-kms-failure-modes job + docs for running locally
chore: tighten timeouts and stabilize tests with deterministic seed + retryable container startup
review_conversation: Rafael Mendes (SRE): Can we ensure the timeout scenario doesn’t hang the job if docker networking flakes? Please add a hard upper bound per test and fail with actionable logs.
Sahana Iyer (author): Added per-test `context.WithTimeout` (20s) and a harness-level watchdog (2m) that dumps the injector config + last 200 proxy events on failure.

Hanae Suzuki (Security): For throttling, please validate we’re mapping to the canonical category name agreed in ENG-4822 (Throttling, not RateLimited). Also confirm we don’t leak provider-specific error text into customer-visible messages in the test assertions.
Sahana Iyer (author): Updated assertions to check `category=Throttling` and only verify internal log fields; no customer-facing strings are asserted.

Allison Grant (Obs): Metric namespacing should match our standard (`redwood.kms.*`). The harness helper currently searches for `kms.client.*` directly; please update to the final names so tests protect us from future renames.
Sahana Iyer (author): Updated to `redwood.kms.client.*` and added a small compatibility shim so the suite fails loudly if names drift.
Diego Santos (Platform): The wall-clock caps seem tight (1.5s) for CI. Suggest bump to 2.5s and assert on retry count + max backoff instead, to avoid flakes.

Sahana Iyer (author): Bumped caps to 2.5s in CI, kept tighter defaults for local runs, and added explicit assertions on attempt count + backoff ceiling. Re-ran suite 20x on CI runner image; no flakes observed.
Tomáš Novák (On-call/runbooks): Can we print the error taxonomy mapping when a test fails? That would help triage quickly.
Sahana Iyer (author): Added failure output showing observed error categories, retry counts, and last span status for the KMS call.
